feature: The Properties pane: clip line and only what is animating
summary: Pick a clip, a title or a sound and the panel now opens on Properties: one line with its name, in, out, length and speed, then Animating, which lists only the values that are keyed. Everything else is behind Animate a property, a grouped picker with a search box.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the sample recording.

try.do: Click the recording's clip on the timeline and read the first line of the panel.
Click Animate a property and pick Opacity.
Click the Opacity diamond while the playhead sits on its key.
Press T, click the picture, type a title and press Command Return.
Animate its Scale and Opacity from the picker, then move the playhead and type a new Scale.
Hover the Scale row and click its cross.
Compare the pane with video.html PROPERTIES (left: mock, right: app).

evaluate: Does the clip line tell you where the thing starts, ends and how fast it plays without looking at the timeline?
Is Animate a property the first place you would look to animate something that is not moving yet?
Does the diamond now behave like Premiere's keyframe button: a key here goes, and where there is none one is written?
Is a cross that only shows on hover enough of a way to stop a value animating, or should it always show?
With Time now holding only Speed and Sound for a clip, is it still worth being its own section?
rough: The dock's section header is the app's own style (title case with the grip), not the mock's small caps title and three dot menu; that is the whole dock, filed as the-dock-headers-match-the-mock-small-caps-title.
The app keeps Premiere's arrows either side of the diamond, which the mock does not draw; the value boxes were widened toward the mock's but stop short of filling the row.
The mock's empty line says 'colours and border width'; the app says 'color and stroke width', the names its own values use, and fits the panel's 60 character line limit.
Animating is a heading inside the pane, not a section of its own that folds, as the mock draws it with a chevron.
A clip's Length row and a title's On screen row are gone from Time, since the clip line says both; a fast stretch says its length and speed (2.0s · 4.0x) but no longer '8s into 2s'.
